summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.4%; weakest: Sugar #11 -16.5%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.92% (-21 bp in a month), 2-year 4.63% (-18 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-3 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.84 (+2.0% in a month, +5.7% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.949 (+18.4% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.677 (-0.0%); USD/MXN 19.14 (+3.9%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -10.9% in a month (+0.9% YTD); VIX 35.9. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 83.41 $/bbl (-12.6% in a month), Brent 89.95, ULSD 3.847 $/gal (-14.2%), natural gas 3.75 (+4.0%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -16.6% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.8%, Hang Seng -5.2%, yuan +0.0% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -11.8% in a month; gold -15.3%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
